evals.query: Create a UserService in my Kora app that depends on a UserRepository.
expected_behavior: Annotates the class with @Component imported from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Gives the class exactly one public constructor taking UserRepository (constructor injection) and stores it in a private final field
Does not claim the class must be final; if it mentions final at all, presents it as a convention and notes that a class carrying an AOP annotation must be non-final in Java / open in Kotlin
Does not use field injection, @Autowired/@Inject-style annotations, or runtime reflection

evals.query: Set up the @KoraApp entry point for a new Kora service that uses HOCON config and Logback logging.
expected_behavior: Declares an interface annotated with @KoraApp (from io.koraframework.common.annotation) that extends HoconConfigModule and LogbackModule
Provides a static main that calls KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Imports KoraApplication from io.koraframework.application.graph
Does NOT import ApplicationGraph — explains it is generated into the application's own package as <KoraAppSimpleName>Graph
States that @KoraApp is only valid on an interface
Does not introduce a runtime DI container, a self-instantiated application class, or a KoraApplication.run overload that takes a config

evals.query: Bootstrap a Kotlin Kora service: the @KoraApp interface, the main function, and the Gradle wiring.
expected_behavior: Declares `@KoraApp interface Application : HoconConfigModule, LogbackModule` with annotations from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Uses a top-level `fun main()` calling KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph) (or KoraApplication.run { ApplicationGraph.graph() })
Sets mainClass to <package>.ApplicationKt, not to the Application interface
Adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:<version>") with an explicit version and notes the ksp configuration is not covered by the kora-bom platform
Adds build/generated/ksp/main/kotlin to the main Kotlin source set
Does not use kapt, and does not use a companion object with @JvmStatic fun main

evals.query: I need to expose a HikariCP DataSource to my Kora container. How do I register it?
expected_behavior: Creates a @Module interface (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Module) with a default factory method returning DataSource
Notes that @Module is valid on interfaces only
Notes that a @Module compiled in the same Gradle module as the @KoraApp is auto-discovered and must not be added to the extends clause
Explains the provider must not return null unless every consumer declares the parameter @Nullable
Does not use @Bean, @Configuration, or @Provides

evals.query: I have two Cache implementations, RedisCache and CaffeineCache, both implementing Cache. How do I inject the Redis one specifically?
expected_behavior: Defines simple marker tag classes (for example RedisTag) and annotates the implementations with @Tag(RedisTag.class) from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Injects with @Tag(RedisTag.class) Cache at the constructor parameter, using the same tag class on both sides

Warns that a tagged component is invisible to an untagged claim, so tagging every implementation and then injecting Cache untagged produces "No component found for dependency" rather than an ambiguity error
Does not use @Qualifier, @Named, or string-based qualifiers

evals.query: I want a NotificationService that fans out to every registered Notifier implementation in the container.
expected_behavior: Injects All<Notifier> from io.koraframework.application.graph in the constructor
States that All<T> extends Iterable<T> — NOT List<T> — and iterates or copies it rather than assigning it to a List field
Mentions @Tag(Tag.Any.class) All<Notifier> is required to also collect tagged components, because a bare All<T> collects only untagged ones
Does not rely on classpath scanning or reflection to discover implementations

evals.query: I'm writing a reusable Kora library module that provides a default ObjectMapper, but the application should be able to replace it.
expected_behavior: Marks the library factory method with @DefaultComponent from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Shows the application overriding it with a plain provider of the same type (no @DefaultComponent)
Explains that when several candidates match, every @DefaultComponent candidate is discarded and the single remaining non-default wins
If it shows an @Override with the same signature, keeps the @Tag on the overriding method and notes that @Override / override is what removes the overridden declaration from the graph
Does not use @Primary, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, or profile-based bean selection

evals.query: How do I break a circular dependency between ServiceA and ServiceB in Kora without restructuring the code?
expected_behavior: Wraps one side as ValueOf<ServiceB> from io.koraframework.application.graph and accesses it via get() when needed
Mentions PromiseOf<T> as the other indirect option, matching the processor's own "Break the cycle with ValueOf<T> or PromiseOf<T>" advice
Does NOT claim ValueOf exposes refresh() — in Kora 2.0 ValueOf declares get(), map() and optional() only
Does not use lazy proxies, setter injection, or reflection to break the cycle

evals.query: A component created by a @Module factory needs init and cleanup hooks. How do I give a factory-built component a lifecycle in Kora?
expected_behavior: Returns Wrapped<T> from the provider and constructs new LifecycleWrapper<>(value, initCallback, releaseCallback)
Imports LifecycleWrapper and Wrapped from io.koraframework.application.graph
Notes that consumers inject the plain T, not Wrapped<T>, because the graph unwraps it
Mentions that a class you own can instead implement Lifecycle with init() and release(), both of which may throw Exception
Does not use @PostConstruct or @PreDestroy, and does not present an async or suspend lifecycle

evals.query: I have a CacheWarmer that must run at startup even though nothing depends on it. How do I force Kora to initialize it?
expected_behavior: Annotates the component (or its provider method) with @Root
Imports @Root from io.koraframework.common.annotation

Explains that graph resolution starts only from @Root declarations, so a component that is neither a @Root nor a transitive dependency of one is absent from the generated graph entirely — with no error to read
Notes that implementing Lifecycle does not by itself make a component a root
Does not use an ApplicationRunner, a CommandLineRunner, or a runtime startup hook

evals.query: We are splitting our Kora service into separate Gradle modules. How do I expose the components of a domain Gradle module to the application module?
expected_behavior: Marks the domain module's interface with @KoraSubmodule from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Has the @KoraApp interface in the assembly module extend the submodule interface, and explains that modules from another Gradle subproject are never auto-discovered

States that the domain subproject needs the annotation processor (io.koraframework:annotation-processors) or KSP processor (io.koraframework:symbol-processors) on its own compile classpath, otherwise the build fails with "Kora submodule was not generated yet"
Mentions that the generated companion is named <InterfaceName>SubmoduleImpl
Uses api rather than implementation for the Kora modules the @KoraSubmodule interface extends

evals.query: My integration test declares `@KoraApp interface TestApplication extends Application` so it can add a test-only repository, but none of the production @Component classes end up in the test graph. The build succeeds. What's wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing -Akora.app.submodule.enabled=true compiler argument (Java) or ksp { arg("kora.app.submodule.enabled", "true") } (Kotlin)
States it must be set on the MAIN compilation, not the test compilation, because it changes what is generated for the production @KoraApp
Explains that this is a silent failure: the processor only emits the warning "Expected @KoraApp as SubModule, but Submodule implementation not found"
Recommends a test that asserts a production component is actually present in the test graph
Does not suggest copying production components into the test sources or duplicating the module list

evals.query: I want Kora to pick RedisCache when cache.redisEnabled is true and CaffeineCache otherwise, decided at startup rather than at build time.
expected_behavior: Uses @Conditional(tag = X.class) from io.koraframework.common.annotation on both implementations, spelling the attribute name `tag =` (Conditional has no value() element)
Publishes a GraphCondition component (io.koraframework.application.graph.GraphCondition) under @Tag(X.class) for each condition
Returns GraphCondition.ConditionResult.matched(reason) / failed(reason) with a reason that names the config key

Explains that both candidates are compiled into the graph and exactly one condition must match at graph initialisation — otherwise NoneOfConditionalNodeMatches or MoreThanOneConditionalNodeMatches at startup
Does not invent a Spring-style @Profile, @ConditionalOnProperty, or a config-keyed annotation attribute
Identifies that @Component, @KoraApp and @Tag do not live in io.koraframework.common in Kora 2.0
Corrects the imports to io.koraframework.common.annotation.{Component, KoraApp, Tag}
Explains that io.koraframework.common holds Configurer, Either, Principal and PromisedProxy, not the DI annotations
Attributes the mistake to a blind ru.tinkoff.kora -> io.koraframework rewrite, which is wrong precisely because 1.x kept these annotations in ...common while 2.0 keeps them in ...common.annotation
Does not claim the original imports are valid

evals.query: After renaming my base package the Kora build fails with errors naming ru.tinkoff.kora classes and old package names that no longer exist anywhere in my source tree. Should I just fix the generated ApplicationGraph by hand?
expected_behavior: Says no — generated sources must never be hand-edited
Identifies stale output under build/generated (build/generated/sources/annotationProcessor/java/main for Java, build/generated/ksp/main/kotlin for Kotlin) as the cause
Prescribes ./gradlew clean classes --no-build-cache (or an equivalent clean plus cache bypass) to regenerate
Explains that any hand-edit is overwritten on the next processor run
Does not suggest adding the generated directory to source control, excluding it from compilation, or editing ApplicationGraph
States that Context no longer exists anywhere in Kora 2.0 — it was removed from the framework, not merely from the HTTP APIs
Removes the Context constructor parameter rather than looking for a renamed or relocated Context type
Explains that nothing can provide it, so the component would fail with "No component found for dependency"
Replaces the behaviour with something explicit (a passed argument, a dedicated component, or MDC/logging where that is what the context was carrying)
Does not invent io.koraframework.common.Context, io.koraframework.common.util.Context, or any other 2.0 Context type

evals.query: Write a Kora 2.0 @Component OrderService with a findById method that returns the order asynchronously, and a Kotlin equivalent.
expected_behavior: Writes a synchronous method returning Order (not CompletionStage<Order>, CompletableFuture<Order>, Mono<Order> or Flux<Order>)
Writes the Kotlin version as a plain `fun findById(...): Order`, not `suspend fun`
States that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous and executed on virtual threads, and that Reactor, CompletionStage and Kotlin suspend were removed as Kora contracts
Does not add a reactive dependency or wrap the result in a reactive type to 'modernise' the code
If asked about real parallelism, points at Java structured concurrency rather than reintroducing reactive types

evals.query: My Kora build fails with: "No component found for dependency: com.example.Cache (no tags)" and a Note section listing com.example.Cache with @Tag(com.example.RedisTag.class). What does that mean?
expected_behavior: Reads the Note section as the answer: a component of the right type exists but carries a tag the injection point does not ask for
Explains the matching rule — an untagged claim never matches a tagged provider
Fixes it by adding @Tag(RedisTag.class) at the injection point (or removing the tag from the provider), rather than by adding a second Cache component
Mentions the other fixes the processor itself suggests: add @Component to an implementation, add a module provider, or extends the module that provides it
Does not suggest disabling the processor, casting, or a runtime lookup

evals.query: Set up build.gradle for a new Java Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Uses the platform io.koraframework:kora-bom, NOT ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent
Declares annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" and wires the koraBom configuration so the processor inherits its version (annotationProcessor.extendsFrom(koraBom))
Sets a Java toolchain of 25 or newer and says Kora 2.0 artifacts are Java 25 class files
Uses io.koraframework coordinates for every Kora dependency and does not reference json-module, cache-redis, database-r2dbc, database-vertx or http-client-async
Adds testAnnotationProcessor when test sources declare Kora annotations
Does not present --enable-preview as a blanket Kora requirement

evals.query: I need the same Kora module wired twice with different config paths — one untagged instance and one tagged instance — without duplicating the provider code. How?
expected_behavior: Uses @FactoryModule (io.koraframework.common.annotation.FactoryModule) on a module method whose return type is itself a module class
Marks the inner providers and their parameters with @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) so they inherit the tag of the enclosing factory-module method
Explains that the tag on the @FactoryModule method propagates to everything that module instance provides, which is how one class yields two non-colliding sets of components
Notes that @FactoryModule must return a class or interface type, and that Tag.Factory outside a factory module is a compile error
Cites a real example such as UndertowPublicHttpServerModule / UndertowSystemHttpServerModule or OkHttpClientModule rather than inventing one

evals.query: Kora 2.0 fails to compile with 'Circular dependency found:'. My @Tag(PluginsEnabled::class) GraphCondition takes All<Plugin> to decide, and each Plugin implementation is @Conditional(tag = PluginsEnabled::class). What is going on?
expected_behavior: Identifies the cycle: the condition depends on every Plugin, and each Plugin depends on the condition through @Conditional

Explains that the processor breaks ordinary cycles with a generated promised proxy for a single component, but never for an All<T>, TypeRef<T> or Graph claim, so a cycle through All<T> is always reported as a circular dependency

Fixes it by removing the back-edge, e.g. making the condition depend on config instead of on the plugins it gates, or moving the shared state into a separate component, and warns that the error's own Fix line 'Use All<ValueOf<T>> or All<PromiseOf<T>> instead of All<T>' does not break this cycle — those are collection claims too and fail with the same error
anti_behavior: Calls the error a Kora internal error or a processor bug
Suggests wrapping the plugins in a lazy wrapper as the fix without checking that the cycle is gone

evals.query: Kora 2.0: I want a component that exists only when a feature flag is on, and a consumer that works with or without it. Is @Conditional on the component plus @Nullable on the consumer's parameter the right design?
expected_behavior: Confirms @Conditional(tag = X.class) on the component with a GraphCondition published under @Tag(X.class) is the gating mechanism

States that since 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #960) a @Nullable (Kotlin T?) or Java Optional<T> dependency on a condition-failed component receives null, so the design works as is; on 2.0.0.RC1 the same dependency throws 'Graph node value was not initialized because condition failed' at startup
Names the RC1-only workaround: All<T> on the consumer (condition-failed members are skipped) or a consumer that is @Conditional on the same tag
anti_behavior: Tells a 2.0.0.RC2 user that @Nullable on a @Conditional dependency still throws and steers them to All<T> as the only option

evals.query: Kora 2.0 Java: OrderService(PaymentService) and PaymentService(OrderService) are both `public final class` @Components. Compilation fails with 'Circular dependency found:' and a Note saying Kora can break a cycle with a proxy only for interface or non-final class dependency. What are my options?
expected_behavior: Explains that the processor breaks a cycle itself by generating a promised proxy when the dependency closing it is an interface (or a non-final class), and reports the error only when it cannot, here because the requested type is a final class
Reads the error sections: the Dependency cycle list ending in [CYCLE], Required at with the parameter that closes the cycle, Note with the reason, and Fix
Recommends depending on an interface implemented by one of the services so the processor can proxy it, or ValueOf<T>/PromiseOf<T> on one side, or extracting the shared state into a separate component
Does not recommend simply removing final from a class whose only constructor takes arguments — the generated subclass proxy then fails to compile
anti_behavior: Says Kora never resolves cycles and a cycle is always a compile error

evals.query: Kora 2.0: to make sure I get the aspect-wrapped instance I wrote a module method `default $UserService__AopProxy userService(...)` and the build now fails with 'Component provider returns a generated AOP proxy type:'. How should this be declared?
expected_behavior: Explains that the AOP proxy is a generated implementation detail and the processors (Java and KSP) reject a provider whose return type is the __AopProxy class

Declares the component (provider return type and every injection point) with the original type UserService; an aspect-annotated @Component UserService is already registered through its proxy by the processor
anti_behavior: Suggests referencing the generated $UserService__AopProxy class anywhere in hand-written code

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0 project: how do I see what the KSP processor did while resolving my @KoraApp graph? In Java I used -AkoraLogLevel=DEBUG.
expected_behavior: Sets the same option through KSP: ksp { arg("koraLogLevel", "DEBUG") } in build.gradle.kts
States that the symbol processors log to the build console like the Java annotation processor, INFO by default
States that KSP writes no build/kora/log file, unlike the Java processor
anti_behavior: Claims koraLogLevel works only for the Java annotation processor
